[GAPS]  
- Serum glucose level — critical to exclude hypoglycemia, a common cause of neonatal lethargy or seizures (though none are present yet).  
- Newborn screening results — required to detect inborn errors of metabolism (e.g., PKU, MCAD, galactosemia) that may be presymptomatic.  
- Total/direct bilirubin — needed to assess for developing hyperbilirubinemia and risk of kernicterus.  
- Blood culture and inflammatory markers (CRP, procalcitonin) — essential to rule out early-onset sepsis, which may lack initial signs.  
- Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4) — to evaluate for congenital hypothyroidism, typically asymptomatic at birth.
